statement: Every company must appoint a company secretary within 6 months of incorporation, and the office cannot be left vacant for more than 6 months; the secretary must be a natural person who meets the local-residency rules and cannot be the same person as a sole director.
caveat: The statutory source is Companies Act 1967 section 171, and the default on the six-month vacancy is a fine on the directors of up to $1,000. Public companies additionally need a secretary with prescribed qualifications; corporate service providers commonly supply the role for startups.
